name: Saints Soter and Caius
history: Two early popes kept together on one day. Soter led the Roman Church around 166 to 175 and was known for its generosity to poorer churches. Caius governed it from 283 to 296, in the years of peace before the great persecution of Diocletian, and was buried in the catacomb of Callixtus. Both are honoured in tradition as martyrs.
life: Little is known of either pope, and the Church honours them for what is certain. Eusebius preserves part of a letter from Dionysius, bishop of Corinth, thanking Soter and the Roman Christians for the alms they sent to churches in need and to Christians condemned to the mines, a custom Dionysius says Rome had kept from the beginning; he adds that Soter wrote to Corinth like a father to his children. Caius, according to the Liber Pontificalis, came from Dalmatia, and later legend made him a relative of the Emperor Diocletian. His tomb was found in the catacomb of Callixtus in the nineteenth century, with part of his epitaph. Whether either man died a martyr is not known for certain; the old calendar honours them as such, and both lived and led their flock when to be a Christian, still more its bishop, was to live under threat.
prayerTo: Saints Soter and Caius, shepherds of the Church of Rome, you cared for poor and distant churches and kept the faith in dangerous times. Pray for the Pope and the bishops, for Christians in need throughout the world, and for me, that I may be generous to those I will never meet. Amen.
penance: Soter’s Church sent alms to Christians far away. Give today to a charity that supports persecuted or poor Christian communities abroad.
meditation: Dionysius thanked Soter for writing to them as a loving father writes to his children. Who needs a letter from you?
prayer: Look forgivingly on thy flock, Eternal Shepherd, and keep it in thy constant protection, by the intercession of blessed Sotérem et Caium and Sotérem et Caium thy Martyrs and Sovereign Pontiffs, whom thou didst constitute Shepherds of the whole Church. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
